LD 1315 - An Act to Authorize the Display of an Inherent Resolve Campaign Medal Decal on a Special Veterans Commemorative License Plate
Good morning, Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Transportation. As you know, my name is Marianne Moore. I proudly
represent Senate District 6 which includes all of Washington County and 16 Communities in Eastern Hancock County as well.
I'm here to introduce LD 1315 - An Act to Authorize the Display of an Inherent Resolve Campaign Medal Decal on a Special Veterans Commemorative License Plate.
Earlier this year I received a letter from a constituent requesting my assistance to add the
Inherent Resolve Campaign Medal (IRCM) to the selection of Veteran Commemorative decals for veteran license plates. Upon visiting the Maine Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV) website, I
discovered a variety of Veteran Commemorative Decal options from World War II European
and Pacific theater campaign medals to the recent operations in Iraq and Afghanistan; however, IRCM was absent.
Operation Inherent Resolve is the ongoing campaign in Iraq and Syria to defeat the Islamic state of Iraq and Syria (ISIS). Operation Inherent Resolve recently passed the 10-year mark, having begun in 2014, exceeding the length of Operation Iraqi Freedom (2003-2011).

The Inherent Resolve Campaign Medal is a United States Department of Defense service award and
campaign medal. The medal was established by Executive Order on March 30, 2016. The medal may be
awarded to members of the U.S. Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Coast Guard, for service in Iraq, Syria, or contiguous waters or airspace retroactively from June 15, 2014, to a date yet to be determined. Service members who were awarded the Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary Medal for
service that is now covered by the Inherent Resolve Campaign Medal may make application to be awarded the Inherent Resolve Campaign Medal in lieu of the Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary
Medal.

This medal is aligned with other medals for which we issue decals that are displayed on Special Veteran
plates.

As a reminder the Special Veteran plate is issued to any person who has served in the United States Armed Forces and who has been honorably discharged, any person who has served a minimum of 20 years in the National Guard and has been honorably discharged or to a person who has served in the United States Armed Forces for at least 3 years and continues to serve. There are 28 Special
commemorative decals that can be issued to applicants awarded the medals, badges or ribbons.
